svg.aria-label: All 46 concepts in the prerequisite cone

path.title: Real number → Real sequence: Real sequence uses Real number in its definition or the chosen account.
σ-algebra → Measure: Measure uses σ-algebra in its definition or the chosen account.
Sum of a nonnegative series → Measure: Measure uses Sum of a nonnegative series in its definition or the chosen account.
Measure → Lebesgue integral: Lebesgue integral uses Measure in its definition or the chosen account.
Measure → Probability space: Probability space uses Measure in its definition or the chosen account.
Probability space → Real-valued random variable: Real-valued random variable uses Probability space in its definition or the chosen account.

Real-valued random variable → Expectation of an integrable real random variable: Expectation of an integrable real random variable uses Real-valued random variable in its definition or the chosen account.
Lebesgue integral → Expectation of an integrable real random variable: Expectation of an integrable real random variable uses Lebesgue integral in its definition or the chosen account.

Expectation of an integrable real random variable → Variance of a real random variable: Variance of a real random variable uses Expectation of an integrable real random variable in its definition or the chosen account.
Variance of a real random variable → Chebyshev's inequality: Chebyshev's inequality uses Variance of a real random variable in its definition or the chosen account.
Set → Function between sets: function requires set in the selected definition or proof. Use the assignment description, rather than requiring a set-theoretic encoding of its graph.
Set → Ordered pair: ordered-pair requires set in the selected definition or proof.
Ordered pair → Cartesian product of sets: cartesian-product requires ordered-pair in the selected definition or proof.
Set → Subset: subset requires set in the selected definition or proof.
Set → Union of a family of sets: union-of-sets requires set in the selected definition or proof.
Set → Intersection of a family of sets: intersection-of-sets requires set in the selected definition or proof.
Subset → Complement of a subset: set-complement requires subset in the selected definition or proof.
Set → Disjoint sets: disjoint-sets requires set in the selected definition or proof.
Function between sets → Bijection between sets: bijection requires function in the selected definition or proof.
Bijection between sets → Finite set: finite-set requires bijection in the selected definition or proof.
Natural number → Finite set: finite-set requires natural-number in the selected definition or proof.
Function between sets → Sequence in a set: sequence requires function in the selected definition or proof.
Natural number → Sequence in a set: sequence requires natural-number in the selected definition or proof.
Cartesian product of sets → Binary relation on a set: binary-relation requires cartesian-product in the selected definition or proof.
Subset → Binary relation on a set: binary-relation requires subset in the selected definition or proof.
Binary relation on a set → Partial order: partial-order requires binary-relation in the selected definition or proof.
Partial order → Total order: total-order requires partial-order in the selected definition or proof.
Partial order → Least upper bound in a partially ordered set: least-upper-bound requires partial-order in the selected definition or proof.
Field → Ordered field: ordered-field requires field in the selected definition or proof.
Total order → Ordered field: ordered-field requires total-order in the selected definition or proof.
Ordered field → Real number: real-number requires ordered-field in the selected definition or proof.
Least upper bound in a partially ordered set → Real number: real-number requires least-upper-bound in the selected definition or proof.
Sequence in a set → Real sequence: real-sequence requires sequence in the selected definition or proof.
Real sequence → Sum of a nonnegative series: nonnegative-series requires real-sequence in the selected definition or proof.
Extended nonnegative real numbers → Sum of a nonnegative series: nonnegative-series requires extended-nonnegative-reals in the selected definition or proof.
Real number → Extended nonnegative real numbers: extended-nonnegative-reals requires real-number in the selected definition or proof.
Real number → Open interval in the real line: open-interval requires real-number in the selected definition or proof.

Function between sets → Binary operation on a set: binary-operation requires function in the selected definition or proof. The source uses binary operations; the short definition is supplied in this catalogue.

Cartesian product of sets → Binary operation on a set: binary-operation requires cartesian-product in the selected definition or proof. The source uses binary operations; the short definition is supplied in this catalogue.
Binary operation on a set → Group: group requires binary-operation in the selected definition or proof. The source assumes the group axioms; the full short definition is supplied in this catalogue.
Group → Abelian group: abelian-group requires group in the selected definition or proof. The additive group is required to be commutative.
Abelian group → Commutative ring with identity: commutative-ring requires abelian-group in the selected definition or proof.
Commutative ring with identity → Field: field requires commutative-ring in the selected definition or proof.

Complement of a subset → σ-algebra: sigma-algebra requires set-complement in the selected definition or proof. Countable unions are indexed by a sequence; closure conditions are part of the definition.

Union of a family of sets → σ-algebra: sigma-algebra requires union-of-sets in the selected definition or proof. Countable unions are indexed by a sequence; closure conditions are part of the definition.
Sequence in a set → σ-algebra: sigma-algebra requires sequence in the selected definition or proof. Countable unions are indexed by a sequence; closure conditions are part of the definition.

σ-algebra → σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets: generated-sigma-algebra requires sigma-algebra in the selected definition or proof. Use the intersection definition; no general topology is assumed.

Intersection of a family of sets → σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets: generated-sigma-algebra requires intersection-of-sets in the selected definition or proof. Use the intersection definition; no general topology is assumed.

σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets → Borel σ-algebra on the real line: borel-sigma-algebra-real-line requires generated-sigma-algebra in the selected definition or proof. Interval generators avoid making general topological spaces a prerequisite for this particular σ-algebra.

Open interval in the real line → Borel σ-algebra on the real line: borel-sigma-algebra-real-line requires open-interval in the selected definition or proof. Interval generators avoid making general topological spaces a prerequisite for this particular σ-algebra.
σ-algebra → Measurable space: measurable-space requires sigma-algebra in the selected definition or proof.
Function between sets → Preimage of a subset under a function: preimage-of-set requires function in the selected definition or proof.
Subset → Preimage of a subset under a function: preimage-of-set requires subset in the selected definition or proof.
Measurable space → Measurable map between measurable spaces: measurable-map requires measurable-space in the selected definition or proof.
Preimage of a subset under a function → Measurable map between measurable spaces: measurable-map requires preimage-of-set in the selected definition or proof.
Disjoint sets → Measure: measure requires disjoint-sets in the selected definition or proof. Countable additivity and the extended nonnegative codomain are definition inputs.

Measurable map between measurable spaces → Real-valued random variable: real-random-variable requires measurable-map in the selected definition or proof. The codomain is the real line with its Borel σ-algebra.

Borel σ-algebra on the real line → Real-valued random variable: real-random-variable requires borel-sigma-algebra-real-line in the selected definition or proof. The codomain is the real line with its Borel σ-algebra.
Complement of a subset → Indicator function of a subset: indicator-function requires set-complement in the selected definition or proof.
Real number → Indicator function of a subset: indicator-function requires real-number in the selected definition or proof.

Measurable map between measurable spaces → Measurable simple real function: measurable-simple-function requires measurable-map in the selected definition or proof. Finite range and the equivalent indicator-sum description are one concept.

Borel σ-algebra on the real line → Measurable simple real function: measurable-simple-function requires borel-sigma-algebra-real-line in the selected definition or proof. Finite range and the equivalent indicator-sum description are one concept.

Finite set → Measurable simple real function: measurable-simple-function requires finite-set in the selected definition or proof. Finite range and the equivalent indicator-sum description are one concept.

Indicator function of a subset → Measurable simple real function: measurable-simple-function requires indicator-function in the selected definition or proof. Finite range and the equivalent indicator-sum description are one concept.

Measurable simple real function → Lebesgue integral: lebesgue-integral requires measurable-simple-function in the selected definition or proof. Use the supremum of nonnegative simple integrals, then positive and negative parts. No convergence theorem is required for this definition.

Lebesgue integral → Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral: integral-monotonicity requires lebesgue-integral in the selected definition or proof. For nonnegative functions, every simple lower approximation to f is also a lower approximation to g.

Lebesgue integral → Linearity of the Lebesgue integral: linearity-lebesgue-integral requires lebesgue-integral in the selected definition or proof. Extend finite linearity from simple functions to the nonnegative integral, then to integrable positive and negative parts.

Linearity of the Lebesgue integral → Variance of a real random variable: variance requires linearity-lebesgue-integral in the selected definition or proof. Finite second moment implies integrability using |x|≤1+x²; no Hölder or Cauchy–Schwarz prerequisite is needed for this route.

Expectation of an integrable real random variable → Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables: markov-inequality requires expectation in the selected definition or proof. Integrate t·1_{Y≥t}≤Y. The integral of the indicator multiple is part of the simple-function integral formula.

Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral → Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables: markov-inequality requires integral-monotonicity in the selected definition or proof. Integrate t·1_{Y≥t}≤Y. The integral of the indicator multiple is part of the simple-function integral formula.

Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables → Chebyshev's inequality: chebyshev-inequality requires markov-inequality in the selected definition or proof. Apply Markov to (X−EX)². Its measurability follows by expressing level events as unions of preimages of real intervals; the elementary calculation stays in this note.

a.title: Chebyshev's inequality If EX²<∞ and t>0, then P(abs(X−EX)≥t)≤Var(X)/t². Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Variance of a real random variable
a.title: Variance of a real random variable If EX²<∞, then Var(X)=E[(X−EX)²]. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables
a.title: Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables If Y is a nonnegative integrable real random variable and t>0, then P(Y≥t)≤E[Y]/t. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Expectation of an integrable real random variable
a.title: Expectation of an integrable real random variable If E abs(X)=∫abs(X)dP<∞, the expectation of X is EX=∫X dP. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Linearity of the Lebesgue integral If f and g are integrable real functions and a,b are real scalars, then af+bg is integrable and ∫(af+bg)dμ=a∫f dμ+b∫g dμ. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral If 0≤f≤g are measurable functions on a measure space, then ∫f dμ≤∫g dμ, allowing infinite integrals. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Real-valued random variable A real-valued random variable is a measurable map from a probability space to ℝ with its Borel σ-algebra. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Lebesgue integral For measurable f≥0, ∫f dμ is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative simple functions below f. For signed f with ∫abs(f)dμ<∞, define ∫f=∫f⁺−∫f⁻. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Probability space A probability space is (Ω,𝔽,P), where 𝔽 is a σ-algebra on Ω and P is a measure on 𝔽 with P(Ω)=1. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Measurable map between measurable spaces A function for which the preimage of each measurable subset of the codomain is measurable in the domain. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Borel σ-algebra on the real line
a.title: Borel σ-algebra on the real line The σ-algebra on ℝ generated by the open intervals. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Measure A measure μ maps a σ-algebra to [0,∞], sends ∅ to 0, and satisfies μ(⋃ₙAₙ)=∑ₙμ(Aₙ) for every pairwise disjoint sequence of measurable sets. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Measurable simple real function A measurable real function with finite range. It can be written as a finite sum ∑ a_i 1_{A_i} with measurable level sets A_i. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Measurable space A set equipped with a specified σ-algebra of subsets. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Preimage of a subset under a function
a.title: Preimage of a subset under a function For f:A→B and E⊆B, f⁻¹(E)={x∈A:f(x)∈E}. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
a.text: Preimage of a subset under a

a.aria-label: σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets
a.title: σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets The smallest σ-algebra containing that family, equivalently the intersection of all σ-algebras on the ambient set that contain it. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Open interval in the real line
a.title: Open interval in the real line For real a<b, the set (a,b)={x∈ℝ:a<x<b}. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
σ-algebra A σ-algebra on Ω contains Ω and is closed under complements in Ω and countable unions. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Sum of a nonnegative series For aₙ≥0, define ∑ₙ≥1aₙ as the supremum of its finite partial sums; the value may be infinite. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Disjoint sets Two sets are disjoint when they have no common element; a family is pairwise disjoint when every two distinct members are disjoint. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Finite set A set X is finite if it is bijective with {1,…,n} for some integer n≥0; its cardinality is n. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Indicator function of a subset For A⊆Ω, the real function 1_A is 1 on A and 0 on its complement. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Function between sets An assignment taking each element of a specified domain set to exactly one element of a specified codomain set. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Subset A⊆B means every element of A is an element of B. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Intersection of a family of sets
a.title: Intersection of a family of sets Inside a specified ambient set, the elements belonging to every member of the family. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Real number A real number is an element of a complete ordered field ℝ; completeness means every nonempty subset bounded above has a least upper bound. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Complement of a subset For A⊆Ω, its complement Ω∖A consists of the elements of Ω that do not belong to A. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Union of a family of sets
a.title: Union of a family of sets The set of elements belonging to at least one member of the family. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
a.text: Union of a family of sets

a.title: Sequence in a set A function from the natural numbers, or the positive natural numbers, to that set. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Real sequence A real sequence is a function a:ℕ₊→ℝ, written (aₙ)ₙ≥1. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

Extended nonnegative real numbers The nonnegative real numbers together with a greatest element ∞. Sums involving ∞ equal ∞, and 0·∞ is taken to be 0 when integrating simple functions. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Set A collection of distinct elements, regarded as one object. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Bijection between sets A function for which each element of the codomain is the image of exactly one element of the domain. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Natural number One of 0, 1, 2, …; natural numbers count finite collections. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Ordered field A field with a total order preserved by addition, in which the product of two positive elements is positive. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

a.aria-label: Least upper bound in a partially ordered set
a.title: Least upper bound in a partially ordered set For A⊆P, its least upper bound is an upper bound s satisfying s≤b for every upper bound b of A, when such an s exists. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Field A commutative ring in which 1≠0 and every nonzero element is invertible. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Total order A partial order in which any two elements are comparable. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Partial order A reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive binary relation, usually written ≤. Immediate prerequisites reviewed

Commutative ring with identity An abelian group under addition, together with an associative commutative multiplication with identity, distributing over addition. The zero ring is allowed. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Binary relation on a set A subset R⊆S×S; writing xRy means (x,y)∈R. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Abelian group A group whose operation is commutative. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Cartesian product of sets A×B is the set of ordered pairs (a,b) with a∈A and b∈B. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Group A set with an associative binary operation, an identity element, and a two-sided inverse for each element. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Ordered pair A pair (x,y) with distinguished first and second entries; (x,y)=(x′,y′) exactly when x=x′ and y=y′. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
Binary operation on a set A function S×S→S. Immediate prerequisites reviewed
